facts.summary: New Mexico's state minimum wage is $12.00 per hour, higher than the federal $7.25.
facts.sourceAgency: New Mexico Department of Workforce Solutions, Labor Relations Division
facts.notes: State rate reached $12.00 on Jan 1, 2023 under 2019 HB 31 with no further statutory increases scheduled; treated as still $12.00 for 2026. Tipped minimum cash wage is $3.00/hr. Several localities (Santa Fe, Albuquerque, Las Cruces, Bernalillo/Santa Fe counties) mandate higher local rates. Could NOT verify the current live figure: DWS pages returned bot-protection rejections and WebSearch budget was exhausted this session. Verify 2026 figure on the DWS Labor Relations minimum wage page.

facts.summary: New Mexico has no daily overtime and no higher salary floor; overtime is 1.5x after 40 hours in a week, mirroring federal law.
facts.sourceAgency: New Mexico Compilation Commission (official NMSA 1978 statutes)
facts.notes: NM requires overtime at 1.5x the regular rate for hours over 40 in a workweek (weekly threshold, same as FLSA); no state daily-overtime rule and no state salary-level test above the federal $684/week. Statute text could not be re-fetched (official statute portal returned 403); verify Section 50-4-22(E) on nmonesource.com.

facts.summary: The New Mexico Human Rights Act protects several classes beyond the federal set, including sexual orientation, gender identity, ancestry, serious medical condition, and spousal affiliation.
facts.citation: NMSA 1978, Section 28-1-7 (New Mexico Human Rights Act)
facts.sourceAgency: New Mexico Compilation Commission (official NMSA 1978 statutes)
facts.notes: Additions beyond the federal Title VII/ADA/ADEA baseline. NMHRA also covers race, color, religion, national origin, sex, pregnancy, age, and physical/mental handicap. Statute text could not be re-fetched (403); verify Section 28-1-7 on nmonesource.com.

facts.summary: The New Mexico Human Rights Act applies to employers with four or more employees, a lower threshold than the federal 15.
facts.sourceAgency: New Mexico Compilation Commission (official NMSA 1978 statutes)
facts.notes: NMHRA defines 'employer' as a person employing four or more persons, extending discrimination coverage below the federal 15-employee threshold. Statute text could not be re-fetched (403); verify Section 28-1-2 on nmonesource.com.

facts.summary: A discrimination complaint must be filed with the New Mexico Human Rights Bureau within 300 days of the alleged discriminatory act.
facts.citation: NMSA 1978, Section 28-1-10(A) (New Mexico Human Rights Act)
facts.sourceAgency: New Mexico Human Rights Bureau (FEPA), NM Dept of Workforce Solutions
facts.notes: State FEPA filing deadline. Statute text could not be re-fetched (403); verify the 300-day period in Section 28-1-10 on nmonesource.com and the filing process on the DWS Human Rights Bureau page.

facts.summary: Actions to recover unpaid wages under the New Mexico Minimum Wage Act must be commenced within three years.
facts.citation: NMSA 1978, Section 50-4-26 (Minimum Wage Act enforcement/limitation); see also Section 37-1-5
facts.sourceAgency: New Mexico Compilation Commission (official NMSA 1978 statutes)
facts.notes: Corrected citation: the three-year statute of limitations for wage claims under Chapter 50, Article 4 is codified in Section 50-4-26 ('a civil action to enforce any provision of Chapter 50, Article 4 NMSA 1978 shall be commenced within three years after a violation last occurs'), not the previously cited Section 50-4-32, which does not exist. The general wage-and-hour limitations statute is Section 37-1-5. Three-year value confirmed via official statute text.

facts.value: New Mexico Whistleblower Protection Act (public employers) plus NMHRA anti-retaliation
facts.summary: New Mexico's Whistleblower Protection Act protects public employees who report unlawful or improper government acts, and the Human Rights Act separately prohibits retaliation against those who oppose discrimination.
facts.citation: NMSA 1978, Sections 10-16C-1 to 10-16C-6 (Whistleblower Protection Act); NMSA 1978, Section 28-1-7(I) (NMHRA retaliation)
facts.sourceAgency: New Mexico Compilation Commission (official NMSA 1978 statutes)
facts.notes: Narrowed sourceUrl from the nmonesource.com portal homepage to the Compilation Commission's own Chapter 10 (Public Officers and Employees) PDF, which contains Article 16C; content could not be re-fetched to confirm the exact 10-16C-1 to 10-16C-6 text (403 to automated fetch on this domain), so this remains unverified -- verify Article 16C therein and Section 28-1-7(I) (Chapter 28) separately on nmonesource.com.

facts.value: discharge: within 5 days (task/piece/commission wages within 10 days); resignation: next regular payday
facts.summary: A discharged employee's fixed wages are due within five days of termination (task- or commission-based within ten days), while an employee who quits is paid by the next regular payday.
facts.sourceAgency: New Mexico Compilation Commission (official NMSA 1978 statutes)
facts.notes: Final-pay timing differs from federal law (FLSA has no final-pay deadline). Statute text could not be re-fetched (403); verify the 5-day/10-day and next-payday rules in Sections 50-4-4 and 50-4-5 on nmonesource.com.
